consequence.statement: Existing SecretStore objects remain stored as v1beta1 until rewritten; a storage version migration and a status.storedVersions update must be done before a later release removes v1beta1.
consequence.remediation: Re-write all SecretStore objects (storage version migration) and update status.storedVersions on the CRD before v1beta1 is removed.

original.statement: The storage version of the secretstores.external-secrets.io CRD moves from v1beta1 to v1, so existing SecretStore objects stay stored as v1beta1 until they are rewritten, and a storage version migration is needed before a later release removes v1beta1.

consequence.statement: SecretStore objects keep working after the upgrade. New writes are stored as v1, and existing objects stay stored as v1beta1 until rewritten. Nothing fails in this release.
consequence.remediation: Plan a storage version migration (rewrite all SecretStore objects) and remove v1beta1 from status.storedVersions on the CRD before upgrading to any release that stops serving v1beta1.

corrected.statement: In 0.16.0 the storage version of secretstores.external-secrets.io moves from v1beta1 to v1 (v1beta1 storage: true → false). v1beta1 is still served, so existing SecretStore objects keep working but stay stored as v1beta1 until they are rewritten.

decision.reason: [ev-f07fad593227] shows only that spec.versions[name=v1beta1].storage on secretstores.external-secrets.io goes from true to false between 0.15.0 and 0.16.0. The validator found v1beta1 is still an API version at the target and is not deprecated [ev-9889c9b8706d][ev-e08924afdc47]. So existing objects keep working in this release, and nothing in the evidence says anything fails, is rejected or must be migrated before or after this upgrade. The storage migration only becomes necessary if a later release removes v1beta1, which makes this review work (behavior-change), not mandatory work (migration-required).
